axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.assessment: All eight original numbered obligations, pilot size/range, browser preference, optional largest-file CLI, owner authority, cost uncertainty and research-only boundary are accounted for. Every exact plan treatment is adjudicated below. No preselected product is imposed; no implementation or live endpoint is required.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential claims: exact subject, operation, version, default, unit, type, domain and exception
axis_coverage.assessment: Independent primary retrieval supports the operation/provider-bound limits, part/page rules, checksum matrix, CORS/expiry, cleanup, conditional writes, rclone defaults and tus/tusd behavior. The final withdraws the unsupported R2 MPU checksum inference and explicitly distinguishes composite SHA256 from full-object CRC. No material unsupported recommendation remains. L1 is a minor wrong release year in all carried TUSD-01 source records.

axis_coverage.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competitors, analogues, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.assessment: Substantive brief-first discovery includes Uppy direct signing, rclone CLI resource/checksum behavior, tus offset resumption and tusd disk-backed S3Store, R2 operation differences, and a released MinIO compatibility chain. Competing routes carry discriminators: direct browser avoids proxying large bytes; CLI adds privilege/support/resource conditions; tus adds an operated server/disk for offset recovery. Opportunities include persistent intent, orphan cleanup, separate unverified-object cleanup, conditional no-overwrite and retry-safe receipt state. This is useful bounded discovery rather than an exhaustive catalogue or generic caution.

axis_coverage.name: Wrong criticism/corrections/rejections and every exact plan disposition
axis_coverage.assessment: C1 is source-correct and already corrected by the draft; final preserves that correction. C2 requests a useful algorithm/type narrowing and final makes it explicitly; the draft had not positively asserted AWS full-object SHA256, so this is an applicability clarification rather than an established false SHA256 claim. C3 properly remains owner-specific uncertainty. No criticism acceptance removes supported optional scope or invents a mandatory product capability. Clause 1/3/4 rejections and clause 2/5/6/7/8 preservation are justified; every exact operative plan treatment is reproduced below. Critic agreement does not validate L1, which the independent reviewer found.

axis_coverage.name: Supported meaning preserved across discovery → draft → critique → final
axis_coverage.assessment: The full final preserves the preferred browser flow, optional largest-file CLI, tus alternative, operation/provider conditions, historical fix, cleanup/duplicates/receipt safeguards, owners/costs and validation status. R2’s false row inference is deliberately removed and disclosed; this is correction, not lost supported scope. The AWS integrity proposal is narrowed to the selected checksum type with conditional whole-file SHA256 readback, avoiding a composite-as-direct-digest error. tusd’s additional buffer/concurrency counts remain in maps while final retains its relevant cap/disk condition; that nonmaterial condensation does not hide or exclude the alternative. A preserved historical lineage error is not a remaining final error.

axis_coverage.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: Proposal/test status is honest: read-only research and artifact procedure/structure checks are reported, all product checks remain NOT_RUN. Proposed checks discriminate endpoint compatibility, browser CORS/signing/expiry, interruption/recompletion, correct/wrong checksums and independent readback, duplicates/DB failure, abort/lifecycle and authorized CLI process boundaries. Observations have relevant oracles: required headers visible, stored length/digest, checksum rejection, parts removed, duplicate policy and no early receipt. Comparator docs, client ETag/part checks, tus per-PATCH checks and hashes of artifacts are not treated as successful archive operation or cryptographic whole-file identity. No deployment test is invented as an obligation.
